1→# Book Reading Leaderboard — Project Plan
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→A real-time leaderboard application that tracks how much time users spend reading. Users pick a display name, start/stop a single reading session at a time (tagged with a book title), and compete on a shared global leaderboard across daily, weekly, monthly, and all-time windows.
     6→

     8→
     9→## Requirements Summary

    12→|---|------------------------------------------|
    13→| Leaderboard metric | Total cumulative reading time            |
    14→| Identity | Username only — no auth, no passwords    |
    15→| Book entry | Free-text title (session label)          |
    16→| Concurrent sessions | One active session per user at a time    |
    17→| Session tracking | Client-side (device clock + local state) |
    18→| Backend role | Sync & leaderboard storage only          |
    19→| Leaderboard scope | Global                                   |
    20→| Leaderboard windows | Daily / Weekly / Monthly / All-time      |
    21→| Leaderboard refresh | REST polling (on tab focus + periodic)   |
    22→| Backend framework | Spring Boot (Kotlin)                     |
    23→| Database | PostgreSQL                               |
    24→| Deployment | Docker Compose (local / self-hosted)     |
    25→| Client UI | Compose Multiplatform (shared UI)        |

   170→
   171→## Database Schema
   172→
   173→```sql
   174→CREATE TABLE users (
   175→    id         BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
   176→    username   TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
   177→    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
   178→);
   179→
   180→CREATE TABLE reading_sessions (
   181→    id           BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
   182→    client_id    TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,   -- client-generated UUID, used for upsert
   183→    user_id      BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
   184→    book_title   TEXT NOT NULL,
   185→    started_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,   -- client-provided timestamp
   186→    ended_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,            -- client-provided; NULL = session still active
   187→    duration_sec BIGINT NOT NULL         -- client-computed and sent on every sync
   188→);
   189→
   190→CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_user    ON reading_sessions(user_id);
   191→CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_started ON reading_sessions(started_at);
   192→CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_client  ON reading_sessions(client_id);
   193→```
   194→
   195→`client_id` is a UUID generated by the client when the session starts. The backend upserts on `client_id`, so repeated syncs (progress updates) update the same row. `duration_sec` is always client-computed — the server never derives it. Leaderboard queries use `WHERE started_at >= :windowStart` on the stored values.
   196→
   197→---
   198→
   199→## REST API
   200→
   201→Base path: `/api/v1`
   202→
   203→### Users
   204→
   205→| Method | Path | Body | Response | Description |
   206→|---|---|---|---|---|
   207→| `POST` | `/users` | `{ "username": "alice" }` | `UserDto` | Register or fetch existing user |
   208→| `GET` | `/users/{username}` | — | `UserDto` | Lookup user |
   209→
   210→### Sessions
   211→
   212→| Method | Path | Body | Response | Description |
   213→|---|---|---|---|---|
   214→| `POST` | `/sessions/sync` | `SessionSyncRequest` | `SessionDto` | Upsert a session by `clientId`; called on start, periodically while active, and on end |
   215→| `GET` | `/sessions/{clientId}` | — | `SessionDto?` | Fetch last-synced state for a session (used on app restore) |
   216→
   217→### Leaderboard
   218→
   219→| Method | Path | Params | Response | Description |
   220→|---|---|---|---|---|
   221→| `GET` | `/leaderboard` | `window=daily\|weekly\|monthly\|alltime` | `List<LeaderboardEntryDto>` | Ranked list of users by total reading seconds |
   222→
   223→---
   224→
   225→## DTO Definitions (`shared-dto`)
   226→
   227→```kotlin
   228→@Serializable
   229→data class UserDto(val id: Long, val username: String, val createdAt: String)
   230→
   231→// Sent by the client on every sync (start, periodic progress, end)
   232→@Serializable
   233→data class SessionSyncRequest(
   234→    val clientId: String,        // client-generated UUID, stable for the session's lifetime
   235→    val username: String,
   236→    val bookTitle: String,
   237→    val startedAt: String,       // ISO-8601, client clock
   238→    val endedAt: String?,        // null while active
   239→    val durationSec: Long        // client-computed elapsed seconds
   240→)
   241→
   242→@Serializable
   243→data class SessionDto(
   244→    val clientId: String,
   245→    val username: String,
   246→    val bookTitle: String,
   247→    val startedAt: String,
   248→    val endedAt: String?,
   249→    val durationSec: Long
   250→)
   251→
   252→@Serializable
   253→data class LeaderboardEntryDto(
   254→    val rank: Int,
   255→    val username: String,
   256→    val totalSec: Long,
   257→    val sessionCount: Int
   258→)
   259→
   260→```
   261→
   262→---
   263→
   264→## Client Screens
   265→
   266→### 1. Home Screen
   267→- Text field: enter username
   268→- "Enter" button → stores username locally, navigates to Session screen
   269→- Shows current active session indicator if one is live
   270→
   271→### 2. Session Screen
   272→- Displays username and currently active session (book title + elapsed timer)
   273→- Timer runs entirely on the device — no network call needed to tick
   274→- "Start Reading" button → input book title → generates `clientId` UUID, starts local timer, persists session to local storage, fires first sync (`POST /sessions/sync`)
   275→- "Stop Reading" button (visible when session active) → stops local timer, sets `endedAt`, fires final sync with `endedAt` populated, clears active-session local state
   276→- Periodic background sync every 30 s while a session is active (keeps leaderboard current)
   277→- Link to Leaderboard screen
   278→
   279→### 3. Leaderboard Screen
   280→- Tab bar: Daily / Weekly / Monthly / All-time
   281→- Ranked list: `#rank · username · Xh Ym` (formatted from totalSec)
   282→- Auto-refresh via REST polling (on tab focus and every 30 s while visible)
   283→- Highlight current user's row
   284→

   291→  db:
   292→    image: postgres:16-alpine
   293→    environment:
   294→      POSTGRES_DB: bookreads
   295→      POSTGRES_USER: bookreads
   296→      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: bookreads
   297→    ports:
   298→      - "5432:5432"
   299→    volumes:
   300→      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
   301→
   302→  backend:
   303→    build: ./backend
   304→    depends_on:
   305→      - db
   306→    environment:
   307→      SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL: jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/bookreads
   308→      SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME: bookreads
   309→      SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD: bookreads
   310→    ports:
   311→      - "8080:8080"
   312→
   313→volumes:
   314→  pgdata:
   315→```

   317→---
   318→
   319→## Implementation Phases
   320→
   321→### Phase 1 — Backend Foundation ✓
   322→- [x] Gradle root project + `backend` and `shared-dto` modules
   323→- [x] Docker Compose with PostgreSQL
   324→- [x] SQL init script: `users` + `reading_sessions` tables (with `client_id` unique column), mounted into the PostgreSQL container
   325→- [x] `UserController` + `UserService` + `UserRepository`
   326→- [x] `SessionController` + `SessionService` (`POST /sessions/sync` upsert on `client_id`, `GET /sessions/{clientId}`)
   327→- [x] `LeaderboardController` + `LeaderboardService` (4 time windows, `SUM(duration_sec)`)
   328→- [x] Integration tests (Testcontainers + PostgreSQL)
   329→
   330→### Phase 2 — KMP Client Scaffold
   331→- [ ] `client` module with all 4 targets (android, iosArm64/iosX64, jvm, Web)
   332→- [ ] Ktor HTTP client wired to backend
   333→- [ ] Platform storage service interface (`LocalStorageService`) with Koin-injected implementations:
   334→  - `androidMain` / `iosMain` / `jvmMain`: `PrefServiceDataStore` backed by `androidx.datastore.core.okio` (`OkioStorage` + JSON serializer + platform `PrefPathProvider`)
   335→  - `webMain`: `PrefServiceLocalStorage` backed by `window.localStorage` (JS interop)
   336→- [ ] `LocalSessionStore` — persists active session state (clientId, bookTitle, startedAt epoch, elapsed offset) across app restarts
   337→- [ ] `SessionSyncService` — fires `POST /sessions/sync`; retries on failure; schedules periodic 30 s sync while active
   338→- [ ] `UserRepository`, `SessionRepository` (client-side), `LeaderboardRepository` (client-side)
   339→- [ ] Koin modules
   340→
   341→### Phase 3 — Compose Multiplatform UI
   342→- [ ] `HomeScreen` with username entry
   343→- [ ] `SessionScreen`: device-local timer via `LaunchedEffect` coroutine ticking every second; start generates clientId + fires first sync; stop fires final sync; timer survives recomposition via `StateFlow`
   344→- [ ] `LeaderboardScreen` with 4-tab view; polls `GET /leaderboard` on tab focus and every 30 s while visible
   345→- [ ] Navigation between screens
   346→
   347→### Phase 4 — Platform Entry Points
   348→- [ ] Android `MainActivity`
   349→- [ ] iOS `MainViewController` + Xcode project skeleton
   350→- [ ] JVM Desktop `main()` with `singleWindowApplication`
   351→- [ ] Web `main()` with `CanvasBasedWindow`
   352→
   353→### Phase 5 — Polish & Packaging
   354→- [ ] Dockerfile for backend (`./gradlew bootJar` → slim JRE image)
   355→- [ ] Error handling: duplicate username, server unreachable (sync queued locally)
   356→- [ ] Sync retry queue: if `POST /sessions/sync` fails, store pending sync in local storage and retry on next connectivity event
   357→- [ ] README with setup and run instructions
   358→
   359→---
   360→
   361→## Key Design Decisions
   362→
   363→**Client owns session lifecycle** — the device starts the timer, owns the `clientId` UUID, and decides when a session ends. No network call is required to begin or resume reading. This means the app works offline; accumulated time is synced when connectivity returns.
   364→
   365→**One active session constraint** — enforced on the client. The client stores at most one active session in local storage. The backend does not check for conflicting active sessions; it blindly upserts on `clientId`.
   366→
   367→**Sync strategy** — the client fires `POST /sessions/sync` on start, every 30 s while active (progress update), and immediately on end. This keeps leaderboard data reasonably current for active sessions without requiring a persistent connection for the timer itself.
   368→
   369→**`duration_sec` is client-authoritative** — the server stores whatever the client sends. The generated-column approach is dropped; `duration_sec` is a plain `BIGINT` column updated on each upsert. This avoids timezone or rounding mismatches between client and server clocks.
   370→
   371→**Leaderboard computation** — computed on read (`SUM(duration_sec)` with `WHERE started_at >= windowStart`), not materialized. Active sessions contribute their last-synced `duration_sec`, so the leaderboard is accurate to within the sync interval.
   372→
   373→**Leaderboard polling** — the client polls `GET /leaderboard` when the leaderboard tab becomes visible and every 30 s while it remains on screen. No persistent connection is required; results are accurate to within the polling interval (same as the session sync interval).
   374→
   375→**Username as identity** — username is stored in a Kotlin `StateFlow` in the client ViewModel and persisted via `LocalStorageService`. On Android, iOS, and JVM, the implementation uses `androidx.datastore.core.okio` (`DataStoreFactory` + `OkioStorage` + JSON serializer); each platform supplies a `PrefPathProvider` (via Koin) pointing to the appropriate files directory. On Web, the implementation writes directly to `window.localStorage` via JS interop. No `expect/actual` is needed — Koin platform modules wire the concrete class.
   376→
   377→**Active session persistence** — the current active session (clientId, bookTitle, startedAt, elapsed offset) is persisted to local storage so a device restart or app kill resumes the in-progress session correctly without data loss.
   378→
   379→**Shared DTOs** — `shared-dto` uses only `kotlinx.serialization` annotations. On the backend, Spring's `ObjectMapper` is configured to delegate JSON to kotlinx-serialization. On the client, Ktor's content negotiation uses the same serialization.
